questions.text: Which planet shares its name with a famous chocolate bar and is known as the Red Planet?
questions.explanation: Mars looks red due to iron oxide on its surface.

questions.text: What is the name of the galaxy that contains our solar system?
questions.explanation: Earth is in the Milky Way galaxy.

questions.text: Who was the first person to walk on the Moon?
questions.explanation: Armstrong stepped onto the Moon on 20 July 1969.

questions.text: Which planet is most famous for its spectacular system of rings?
questions.explanation: Saturn's rings are the most extensive and visible.

questions.text: What is the closest star to Earth?
questions.explanation: The Sun is about 150 million kilometres away.

questions.text: Which planet in our solar system is the hottest?
questions.explanation: Venus's thick atmosphere traps heat, making it hotter than Mercury.

questions.text: Who was the first human to travel into space, in 1961?
What was the name of the Apollo 11 lunar module?
questions.explanation: The lunar module Eagle landed in the Sea of Tranquility.

questions.text: Which Italian scientist first observed the four largest moons of Jupiter in 1610?
questions.explanation: Galileo discovered Io, Europa, Ganymede and Callisto.

questions.text: Which is the largest planet in the solar system?
questions.explanation: Jupiter is more massive than all other planets combined.

questions.text: What is the largest moon of Saturn?
questions.explanation: Titan is Saturn's largest moon and has a thick atmosphere.

questions.text: Which comet returns to the inner solar system roughly every 76 years?
What was the name of the first artificial satellite, launched in 1957?
questions.explanation: The USSR launched Sputnik 1 in October 1957.

questions.text: Which astronomer formulated three laws of planetary motion?
questions.explanation: Kepler showed planets move in elliptical orbits.

questions.text: What is the name of the boundary around a black hole beyond which nothing can escape?
questions.explanation: Nothing crossing the event horizon can return.

spares.text: What force keeps the planets in orbit around the Sun?
spares.explanation: The Sun's gravity holds the planets in orbit.

spares.text: Who was the first American to orbit the Earth?
Which mission first carried humans around the Moon, in December 1968?
spares.explanation: Apollo 8 orbited the Moon ten times.
